today.hard: The old game (balanceRev 4): 2, 3, 4, 5 weights to hang (1, 2, 3, 3 fixed) on 8, 8, 8, 10 notches; hang limits 9, 12, 15, 18; 120 s
today.expert: 4 scales of 10 notches; 3, 4, 5, 6 weights to hang (1, 2, 2, 2 fixed); 5, 6, 6, 7 spare hangs; balance readout hidden; 120 s

measured: Not documented. This session's read-only kit run (24 deals, medians for the average / good / great / near-perfect kit): Easy 197 / 200 / 200 / 200; Normal 95 / 194 / 200 / 200; Hard 94 / 170 / 189 / 200; Expert 31 / 62 / 94 / 171 (79 % finish). Hard scores like Normal.

glance.easy: A short six-notch beam and two light weights
glance.hard: A long ten-notch beam with two weights already hung
glance.expert: Ten notches, three weights to hang, no balance readout

why: Every weight is a torque sum, so a longer beam and more weights multiply the sums, and hiding the readout last makes the player do them in the head.
proof: Each scale is proved balanced with both sides used and, where set, exactly one arrangement (balancedArrangements, exhaustive) when dealt. Expert keeps only scales personSolveScale (balanceLevels.server.ts) balances without the readout inside 40 trial hangs. scripts/number-levels-balance-target-check.ts pins it. New Hard: the same filter with the readout on, and the near-perfect kit finishing 95 % or more inside 120 s.
stamp: Level field only: balanceRev 5 already stores each deal's scales, hang limits and hideBalance. Hard moves from balanceRev 4 to a balanceRev 5 settings row, so its practice bests restart.
risk: It retires the old game from Hard, which Joe chose on 15 Nov; the kits show that Hard scoring like Normal (average 94 against 95).

name: Exact
lever: Targets to hit in the round

today.easy: 6 numbers, 1 or 2 big (25, 50, 75, 100); target 101 to 300 that 3 or 4 numbers make; 75 s
today.normal: 6 numbers, 1 or 2 big, small ones 1 to 10; target 101 to 999; 75 s; full speed points by 30 s
today.hard: Exactly 1 big number; target 300 to 999 that needs all six; 75 s
today.expert: No big number; target 500 to 999 that needs all six, from a bank of 320 boards a person-like solver cracks; 75 s

measured: Not documented. This session's kit run (24 deals; the kit's search time is set by level name): Easy 189 / 200 / 200 / 200; Normal 168 / 194 / 200 / 200; Hard 52 / 78 / 120 / 180; Expert 26 / 52 / 78 / 173 (83 % finish). The scores step, but all four screens look the same.
easy: 1 target of two digits (20 to 99) that 2 or 3 of the six numbers make, 2 big numbers on the rack, 75 s.
hard: 2 targets in a row, each on a fresh rack, 100 s: first a Normal-style target, then today's Hard board (1 big number, 300 to 999, needs all six). Points per target; full speed points by 50 s.
expert: 3 targets in a row, 120 s: a Normal-style target, then 1 big number needing five or six, then today's Expert board (small numbers only, 500 to 999, needs all six). Full speed points by 75 s.
why: One deep target is all or nothing and looks the same at every level, so the harder levels chain targets that rise inside the round: the load doubles, then trebles, and an average player still banks the first.
proof: Each target is proved by exhaustive search to need its count of numbers (targetLevelRoute, targetLevels.server.ts). Expert's last target comes from the existing proved bank (targetExpertBank.server.ts, scripts/target-expert-bank.ts, personSolveTarget). To write: a bank of whole rounds per level, and a check that the near-perfect kit finishes 80 % of Expert rounds inside 120 s (my estimate from today's times: about 16 + 35 + 60 s).
newMechanic: Targets in a row: 2 at Hard, 3 at Expert, announced as "Target 1 of 2" with the Number family's stage pips. Arrives at Hard.
stamp: New stamp (for example targetRev 1): the stored puzzle holds 2 or 3 racks and targets and the grader pays per target. Today's one-target rounds grade as before.
risk: The biggest build of the group: a staged screen, answer format, grader and reveal for a game with one board today.

glance.hard: Four numbers and three empty circles

Add an assertion that no level ever deals a fallback equation.
